title: Stream-preserving weighted traffic shift protocol
creator: Ava Martinez
summary: Design and implement a weighted traffic-shift protocol that preserves active streaming sessions and token continuity during active-active regional failover while respecting SLOs and upstream circuit-breakers.
description:
Problem: Hosted API customers depend on long-lived streaming sessions and KV-backed prefix caches. During an active-active multi-region failover or load-shedding event we must shift traffic away from an overloaded region without truncating client streams, losing KV state, or violating latency and availability SLOs. Existing shift controllers are epochal and drop transient streams or cause duplicated tokens where clients re-connect to a different region.

Goal: Implement a shift protocol (Shiftstone) that performs incremental, weighted traffic redirection with a short-lived stream proxy/handshake to preserve session continuity, token ordering, and KV cache validity. The protocol must interoperate with per-route circuit-breakers and tiered load-shedding policies, be observable (traceable across regions), and provide automated rollback on SLO regressions.

Non-goals: Full cross-region KV replication; we will rely on short-lived proxy handshakes and cache warmup rather than synchronous state mirroring in this iteration.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Shiftstone can move 100% of a route's new connections from region A to region B in controlled increments (0-100) while active streams started in A are proxied to B and complete without token loss.

2) During a shift, 99th percentile streaming tail latency for preserved sessions increases by no more than 20% compared to baseline, and availability meets the route SLO (99.9% for control plane measurable requests).

3) Circuit-breaker interplay: if region B tripped its circuit-breaker during a shift, Shiftstone automatically pauses increases, reduces incoming weight, and falls back to a safe routing policy within 10s.
4) Load-shedding hooks: Shiftstone honors per-tenant and per-route shedding directives; shed tokens are dropped with clear error codes and clients receive a canonical retry hint.
5) End-to-end telemetry exists: per-shift trace IDs, token-preservation audit events, and per-region metrics are emitted and visible in a dashboard runbook.
6) Automated canary: Run a 1% canary for 30m with synthetic streaming probes that validate token continuity before expanding traffic.
7) Chaos test: Simulate region A abrupt failure and verify Shiftstone completes handoff for in-flight streams within 60s for >=95% of sessions in integration tests.
8) Security review completed and KMS/HSM secrets used for any inter-region handshake tokens.
tasks: Design protocol sequence diagram: client handshake -> edge proxy -> region B connector -> KV cache warmup -> token stitching
Implement short-lived stream proxy component (stateless control-plane auth + ephemeral data-plane tunnel), with size-limited buffer and backpressure semantics
Extend gateway routing layer to accept fractional weights and expose per-route shift state to the control plane
Add circuit-breaker callbacks to shift controller: on-trip pause/reduce/backoff policies
Implement load-shedding integration: honor tenant-level quotas and produce standard HTTP/gRPC error codes with retry-hint headers
Instrument trace IDs and add Shiftstone panels to Console: shift timeline, preserved-session count, token-loss rate
Create automated canary job with streaming synthetic probes and alerting thresholds
Write e2e integration tests including abrupt region failure, high-latency tails, and KV warmup regressions
Perform security review for ephemeral token exchange and update runbook
Document operational playbook and rollback steps in Confluence and link runbook to on-call Slack channels
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): implement unit tests and simulate single-region weighted shifts in local harness
Phase 1 (staging): deploy Shiftstone on staging with 1% canary across two regions; run synthetic streaming probes for 48h
Phase 2 (limited): enable for selected low-impact routes and partners (5%) for 7 days; monitor telemetry and error budgets
Phase 3 (gradual): widen to 25% then 50% in 24h increments if SLOs hold; otherwise rollback to previous weights
Phase 4 (on-demand): enable as an operator tool for incident-driven failover and as a default for scheduled maintenance
Emergency path: immediate traffic diversion via legacy region fencing if Shiftstone health crosses critical thresholds
metrics_and_triggers: Primary SLOs: request success >= 99.9% (control path), streaming tail p99 latency <= baseline * 1.2
Shift progress trigger: increase weight step only if preserved_session_error_rate < 0.1% and p99 latency delta < 15% for 5m
Pause/backoff trigger: if region-targeted circuit-breaker trips OR preserved_session_error_rate > 0.5% OR p99 latency delta > 25%
Auto-rollback: if error budget burn rate exceeds 10x in a 30m window, revert to last known-good weights
Observable counters: preserved_sessions, proxied_bytes, token_stitch_success, token_stitch_failure, kv_warmup_hit_rate
notes: We intentionally avoid synchronous cross-region KV replication in this phase; instead we use a cache-warmup handshake to reduce tail misses.
Short-lived proxy introduces additional hops; we cap buffer sizes and prefer in-place streaming where possible to avoid amplification.
Expect coordination with networking (VPC peering / egress rules) and infra for ephemeral tunnels across regions.
UX: Console will show active preserved-session counts and an option to visualize per-session latency impact during a shift.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Ava Martinez: Initial ticket created after on-call incident where abrupt capacity loss in us-east caused truncated streams for a major customer.

2026-03-11 - Daniel Cho: Spike completed; prototype proxy can handshake and forward a live stream with token continuity in the lab. Observed 8-12% p99 increase when proxying across regions but no token loss.
2026-03-12 - Priya Nair: PM review - ask for explicit per-tenant opt-out and clearer client error codes for shed tokens. Added to tasks.

implementation_notes: Favor gRPC bidi streams for proxy tunnels where client supports them; fallback to chunked HTTP for older clients.
Token stitching approach: generate short-lived continuation token signed by origin region KMS and validated by target region during handshake.
Backpressure: if target region reports congestion, proxy should signal clients to reduce rate or produce a controlled EOF with retry hint.
Testing harness: extend existing streaming integration test suite to inject network partitions and asymmetric latency profiles.
